questions: evaluation/memorybench/longmemeval-stratified30-v1.json (first five per category of the stratified sixty; extendable to the full sixty by resuming)

arms.llm-memory-store-raw: existing completed run llm-memory-store-longmemeval-stratified60-v1 (vector recall, ranked-v1, top ten raw messages), restricted to the thirty questions

metric: answer-content presence (scripts/score_content_answer_presence.py): normalized gold answer contained in the retrieved text, exact containment for answers of at most two content tokens, otherwise at least 80% of answer tokens present. A lexical floor on answer availability; not answer quality.

views.supermemory-local-top10: first ten Supermemory results (memories plus any chunks): matched depth with the store
views.supermemory-local-full: every returned result, as MemoryBench's Supermemory prompt presents them: Supermemory's own default

reported: hits overall and per category for every arm and view
median retrieved context characters per arm and view
paired discordant counts and a two-sided sign test, store versus supermemory-local-top10
ingest failures and extraction time per session
disclosed_asymmetries: Supermemory is designed for a strong hosted extraction model; this measures it under a free local 7B model, as the earlier Mem0 OSS comparison measured Mem0
the store stores raw messages and needs no extraction model
Supermemory embeds with bge-base (768d), the store with bge-small (384d)
the store run predates this comparison and is reused unchanged
claim_scope: On these thirty LongMemEval-S questions, under free local models only, the store's top ten contained the gold answer text in X cases and Supermemory Local's in Y. No claim about Supermemory's hosted service, answer quality, or other configurations.
